text:
Aisha Khan: Hey folks, new here. Trying to spin up local stack (postgres+redis) with docker-compose on an M1 Mac. Postgres container exits with permission denied writing to /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata. Init SQLs aren't running. Any quick dev-friendly fixes?

Tom Wu: Welcome! Most common is bind-mount ownership. Quick test: sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ./pgdata && docker-compose up postgres. Alternatively use a named volume to avoid host perms.

Aisha Khan: I switched to a named volume and it starts, but my app on host still can't connect unless I expose port. Is host.docker.internal preferred?

Tom Wu: Yes for host apps on mac use host.docker.internal:port. If you don't want to expose 5432 (conflicts with homebrew postgres), map to a high port like 15432:5432 and point your app to host.docker.internal:15432.

infra-helpers-bot: Note: dev docs at https://redwood.internal/dev/local-db-setup include recommended compose overrides and .env.local.template.

Aisha Khan: One last thing: my init scripts didn't run even after nuking volumes. They were mounted as 0640. Changed to 0644 and re-created volume, now they run. Thanks!
